sections.heading: How NEET preparation is structured here
body: NEET is an NCERT-first examination — the large majority of questions, especially in Biology, trace directly to textbook lines, tables and diagrams. Our track is built around that fact: notes map each chapter to its NCERT source with high-yield lines flagged, practice questions cite the lines they test, and revision capsules compress the most repeated facts for the final month.

Biology carries half the paper and rewards precise reading; Chemistry splits between NCERT-line Inorganic, mechanism-logic Organic and numerical Physical; Physics rewards formula fluency plus assertion-reason practice. Subject pages lay out the chapter order that respects these differences.

sections.heading: Reading NCERT the NEET way
body: Passive reading fails NEET aspirants because the paper tests exact lines — examples, exceptions, scientist names, data values. Read each chapter with a pen: underline every exception (the paper loves them), convert tables into self-quizzes, and redraw every diagram from memory with labels.
After reading, immediately attempt the chapter's practice questions and PYQs. Anything you miss points back to a specific NCERT paragraph — that paragraph, not a new book, is the remedy.

sections.heading: Mocks and the final 30 days
body: NEET mocks train three things: 200-minute stamina, OMR accuracy under pressure, and the discipline to skip time-sinks. Analyse every mock the same day — categorise errors into knowledge gaps, silly mistakes and time losses, and fix each category differently.
In the last month, stop adding new material. Cycle revision capsules, re-solve flagged PYQs, and keep one-line-per-chapter recall sheets that you can finish the morning of the exam.

faqs.question: Is NCERT enough for NEET?
faqs.answer: For Biology, NCERT plus rigorous practice covers the vast majority of the paper. Physics and Chemistry need NCERT plus structured problem practice — which is exactly how this track is organised.

faqs.question: How should I split time between Biology, Physics and Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Roughly in paper proportion with a tilt toward your weakest subject: many toppers use 40-25-35 across Biology, Physics and Chemistry, adjusted monthly by mock analysis.

faqs.question: When should I start full-syllabus mocks?
faqs.answer: After one complete syllabus pass with chapter-wise practice — typically with 3–4 months left — then weekly, moving to twice-weekly in the final month.
